source: no published source; read from the installed 2.0.1 plugin.dylib

lines: A multiple: one voltage copied to three jacks, twice over, with the second group fed from the first until its own source jack is used
The voltage copied to Ports 2, 3 and 4, and to Ports 6, 7 and 8 as well while Port 5 is empty
A copy of whatever is patched to Port 1, at the same number of channels, and one channel of 0V while Port 1 is empty
The voltage copied to Ports 6, 7 and 8; putting a cable in here cuts that group off from Port 1
A copy of Port 5, or of Port 1 while Port 5 is empty, at the same number of channels, and one channel of 0V while both are empty
Note — the small triangle drawn between the fourth and fifth jacks marks the break: Port 1 feeds both groups until something is patched to Port 5.
Note — both groups pass polyphony straight through, so a sixteen-channel cable into Port 1 comes out of all six copies with sixteen channels.
Note — the jacks carry no printed names; hovering one shows the maker's own numbering, Port 1 through Port 8, counted downwards.

0.why: plugin.dylib AI001Module::process at 0x3af4: the channels byte of inputs[0] (Module+0x38, +0x40) becomes the bound of an unrolled 16-float copy loop into outputs[0], outputs[1] and outputs[2], and the same count is written to each output's channels byte

1.why: plugin.dylib AI001Module::process at 0x3ed8: cmp of the inputs[1] channels byte selects an offset of 0 or 0x50 into the input array, so the second group's source is inputs[1] when it has channels and inputs[0] when it has none; the chosen port's voltages are then copied into outputs[3], [4] and [5]

AI001_Multiple.notes: No source is published for this plugin; everything here was read out of the installed 2.0.1 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped and holds one AI001Module::process. The jacks carry no family: a multiple passes on whatever is patched into it, so no colour is the honest answer. The port names in the lines are the maker's own configInput and configOutput strings, which are in the binary as "Port 1 (source)", "Port 5 (source / break)" and "Port 2" through "Port 8"; nothing is lettered on the panel itself. The only context-menu item is "Panel skin", offering "Black" and "Silver" and saved to the patch as panelSkin; it changes which of res/AI001-black-v6.svg and res/AI001-silver-v6.svg is drawn and nothing else, so it is left out of the lines. An unpatched source leaves its three outputs at one channel of 0V rather than disconnected: process() writes the channel count 1 and a zero voltage. No numeric constants are quoted in any line, so check_numbers.py has nothing to test here.
